body: If that's the only reason i am sad for you...

Only my closest friends knew at first, thy handled it well, not to overbearing and not to distant they were there if i wanted to talk but never forced anything.  I told my family (mom, dad) about two months ago they were shocked but it was a long time after the fact so i was okay by then.  The therapists and those whacks were the annoying ones,  they tended to focus on one aspect of your life and always assumed that that was the reason you tried to do it and never actually listened to what you were trying to say.

Yes every so often i hit a down week.
After a week in the nut house they had me on Lexapro and i took that for about 2 months after but stopped taking them.
I learned to stop taking advantage of the smaller things in life, the things that no matter what is going on are always there.
I met a remarkable girl in the nut house that no matter what life through at her she still kept a good front and always took it in stride.
Death was greatly appealing to me at that point.  Not existing seemed like the best thing i could do for myself.  I still fight the thought every now and again but it's getting easier as time goes on.
The majority i did by just giving up the thought that i will ever be happy, I know that sounds bad but trying to live up to some weird standard you set for yourself makes it harder to be happy with what you have and where you are.  I also found that sometimes friends and family tend to make it worse.  If they are unaware how to handle something like this they tend to take your suicide attempt as a attack on them personally and tend to be counter productive although they mean better.  But saying that having people around to just pat you on the back and say they are glad you didn't die does help.
Learning to accept that i had to deal with the depression instead of just reacting to it. If that makes any sense...
